title: flydubai Flight 1073
subtitle: Dubai → Tel Aviv, diverted to Tabuk
note: A reconstruction from the aircraft's own ADS-B broadcasts of what Israel calls an attempted suicide terror attack, in which everyone aboard survived. The take-off roll and the last half hour before landing rest on few positions and are partly reconstructed; the Saudi and UAE investigations have not concluded.
summary: flydubai 1073, a Boeing 737 MAX 8, from Dubai to Tel Aviv on 30 September 2026 with 174 passengers, most of them Israelis.

Over northern Saudi Arabia the first officer stabbed the captain and the aircraft dived from 34,000 to 16,600 ft in about a minute, far past its speed limits. The wounded captain opened the cockpit door; cabin crew and passengers overpowered the attacker, and two off-duty flydubai pilots flew on and landed at Tabuk at about 06:45 UTC.

Israel's assessment: an attempted jihadist suicide attack by a first officer radicalized over the past year, acting alone. Saudi Arabia's preliminary inquiry found he assaulted the captain; the UAE is investigating a terrorist link.

card.title: flydubai Flight 1073
lines: 30 September 2026 · Boeing 737 MAX 8 A6-FKF, Dubai to Tel Aviv, 174 passengers and 6 crew.

The first officer stabbed the captain and the aircraft dived. Cabin crew and passengers broke into the cockpit and overpowered him; two off-duty flydubai pilots landed it on runway 31 at Tabuk at about 06:45 UTC. Everyone aboard survived; the captain, Smit Machchhar, is recovering from his wounds.

Israel calls it an attempted jihadist suicide attack by a first officer radicalized over the past year. Saudi Arabia's preliminary inquiry found he assaulted the captain; the UAE, which now holds him, is investigating a link to terrorism. There is no official finding on the motive yet.

From the aircraft's ADS-B broadcasts as received by adsb.lol (ODbL) and, where no open network heard it, by other receivers and published tracking data. The take-off roll and the 15 minutes before the final approach are reconstructed.

sources.title: adsb.lol, the day's ADS-B trace of 8965D1 (A6-FKF), trace_full_8965d1.json, fetched 2026-09-30 08:31 UTC

The aircraft's own GPS positions (NACp 8–9), pressure and GNSS altitude, airspeed, Mach, ground velocity, selected altitude and heading, squawk and emergency status, ~1 Hz where received. track.csv smooths them (tools/scenarios/fz1073/reconstruct.ts); rows marked A are within 5 s of a reception.

sources.title: Israel's assessment: Prime Minister Netanyahu (Fox News, 1 October), Defence Minister Katz (30 September), Israeli intelligence officials (N12, 1–2 October)
sources.note: The first officer underwent Islamist radicalization over the past year, acted alone and meant to bring the aircraft down; Netanyahu: "clear he was suicidal"; Katz: "an attempted jihadist terror attack". Israeli officials found no Iranian involvement so far. An assessment, not an investigation's finding.

sources.title: Saudi Interior Ministry, preliminary inquiry (1 October), and the UAE Attorney General's investigation (1 October)
sources.note: Saudi Arabia: "the pilot was assaulted by his co-pilot, resulting in various injuries to both". The UAE, which received the first officer from Saudi Arabia on 2 October, is examining a possible connection to terrorist activity or intent and prior planning.

sources.title: News reports, 30 September–2 October 2026 (passenger accounts in ABC News and CBS News; The Times of Israel's photos of the tail; The Aviation Herald; flydubai's statements)
sources.note: Passengers: the wounded captain released the cockpit door; cabin crew and passengers overpowered the first officer, one passenger pulled back on the controls, and two off-duty flydubai pilots took over and landed. Photos at Tabuk: much of the rudder missing (The Times of Israel, 30 September). flydubai: the aircraft was "secured by on-duty flydubai crew travelling on the flight".
